environment.parallelLoad: dashboard snapshot worker thread (in-process, started by this run); operator report: none - quiescent Windows desktop, no other benchmark or test job running

stageAccounting.note: localProcessingMs is the wall clock from the mocked RPC answers being complete to the accepted transaction being durable: storing the raw batch, resolving the chain time, writing the artifact, deriving the projection, the windows, the valuations and the signals, and committing them. Every stage inside it is measured once and they partition that one window, so their sum is at most it. rpcAcquisition and notify stand outside it. networkWaitMsAfterFetch is the part of the window that was spent inside the transport rather than computing, and the background metadata apply is inside it by construction: its CPU is this process's work while its network is not counted in any stage.

boundary.network: mocked in process: fetch answers JSON-RPC from a synthetic chain
boundary.provider: none: no HTTP request leaves this process
boundary.pacing: the mock reader runs unpaced and unbudgeted; config/robinhood.json pacing unexercised
boundary.database: temporary SQLite under the OS temp directory, removed at exit
boundary.clock: wall clock, so RSS and the dashboard worker thread are part of the measurement

filterPlan.strategy: pool-ids (the live default; the manager experiment is not wired into production)

http.note: A summary GET answered from the published snapshot: the request asks for a newer generation and is answered from what is published now rather than waiting for one.
